newsitem.title: USA: US Forest Service chief Thomas resigning.
newsitem.headline: US Forest Service chief Thomas resigning.

text.p: U.S. Forest Service chief Jack Ward Thomas will step down in mid November to take a job teaching at the University of Montana, the U.S. Agriculture Department said Thursday.
A successor has not been named.

"I look forward to returning to the West. That's where my heart is," Thomas said in a statement. "Now that I have fulfilled my personal and professional goals with the Forest Service, I look forward to this new challenge."
Thomas was the first wildlife biologist to head the agency, which oversees 191.6 million acres of national forest and grasslands.
He was appointed to the post by President Clinton in 1993 after playing a lead role in how to save the spotted owl from extinction.
As head of the Forest Service, Thomas got caught in the middle of the controversy between environmentalists and the timber industry over how to manage the nation's forests.
